name: ShowTrust
subcategory: hosted collection page + embeddable wall of love, installable by an AI agent
tagline: A shareable link that collects testimonials, and a widget an agent can install for you

pricing.notes: Free covers one project with unlimited testimonials · 4.99/mo (or 49.99/yr) adds one more project and nothing else · no feature is locked behind the paid tier

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: Unlimited testimonials; 1 project; no visitor/page-view cap; no watermark.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: Unlimited testimonials and usage; paid project/features bundle.

pricing.freeTierCaps: Unlimited testimonials; 1 project; no visitor/page-view cap; no watermark.

verdictSummary: A submission form, an approval queue, and a grid of cards you can embed elsewhere. There is no algorithm here and no network effect · an agent will produce a working version in one sitting, same as it will for the $25 and $29 tools in this category. The catch is the same one Eloqra has: the hosted version is free for a single site, with no cap on testimonials, so you'd be spending a weekend and a hosting bill to replace zero dollars. Worth building if you want the data on your own box or you enjoy the exercise. Not worth building to save money, because there isn't any to save.
coreLoopDIY: A public page collects a name, photo, star rating and quote; you approve them; approved ones render as an embeddable wall on your site.
requirements: somewhere to put uploaded avatars (local disk is fine)
whatYouLose: a free tier · one site with uncapped testimonials costs nothing hosted, so the DIY build starts out behind on price

the install itself · an agent can provision the account from your email alone, get working credentials in the same response, create the project and paste the snippet into your framework, with the human only clicking a claim link afterwards · your own build is something you have to go and deploy
the design surface you'd otherwise hand-build · multiple layouts, eight card styles, colour palettes, and sliders for width, spacing and radius, all previewable instead of CSS-tweaked by hand
did-it-work data · impression and CTA-click tracking with click-through rate and which domains your wall is actually being viewed on
X-verified testimonials · an OAuth flow that reads X's own verified state, so the quote is provably tied to a real handle and avatar
whyPeopleStillPay: For one site, they don't · it's free, uncapped, and nothing is feature-gated, so the paid tier only exists to add a second project. What you actually trade away by self-hosting is smaller and more boring than money: the layout and styling controls are a real chunk of fiddly frontend work, and the impression tracking tells you whether the wall is doing anything at all, which a hand-rolled version silently won't. One honest mark against the hosted option · the collection page carries a 'Powered by ShowTrustTo' line on every tier, paid included, and there's no switch to remove it. If that badge on a page you send to customers bothers you, that alone is a legitimate reason to build your own.

alternatives.name: Real Testimonials
alternatives.desc: Another WordPress route: forms, moderation, grids and sliders are free; video and the clever automation live upstairs.

facts.install: Install and activate the plugin from WordPress Plugins → Add New
facts.dataFormat: Testimonials, form submissions and display settings live in the site's WordPress database; reviewer images and other uploaded media live in the WordPress media library
facts.gapVsPaid: It only becomes simple after you already run WordPress, and it lacks ShowTrust's hosted share link and agent-assisted installation on an arbitrary site.
facts.setupBlocker: It only works inside a self-hosted WordPress site, so a non-WordPress site first needs an entire WordPress installation

alternatives.name: Shosay
alternatives.desc: Unlimited text, video and audio proof, imports, walls and 25-plus widgets; the bill is zero, the tiny Powered by pill is not.

facts.install: Hosted signup, then paste an iframe/widget embed into the site
facts.dataFormat: Testimonials and account data live in Shosay's hosted PostgreSQL service, while uploaded images/media use Cloudflare R2; users can export their testimonials
facts.gapVsPaid: It provides a generous hosted collector and widgets, but the free badge remains visible and installation, styling and site placement are still your responsibility.
facts.setupBlocker: You need permission to paste Shosay's embed code into the site, and every free widget carries a small Powered by Shosay pill

alternatives.name: Strong Testimonials
alternatives.desc: A WordPress-only form, moderation queue, grid, slider and widget; simple enough once you already own the WordPress problem.

facts.install: Install and activate from WordPress Plugins → Add New
facts.dataFormat: Testimonials and front-end form submissions live in the site's WordPress database; images use the site's WordPress media storage, and optional notification emails can contain submitted fields
facts.gapVsPaid: It requires a self-hosted WordPress site and lacks ShowTrust's universal hosted collection link and done-for-you widget installation.
facts.setupBlocker: It requires a self-hosted WordPress site; the free edition has one collection form and lacks built-in captcha, so public forms may need another anti-spam layer

rejectedAlternatives.name: Reviewskits
rejectedAlternatives.desc: A young headless stack with 52 stars, no releases, and an SDK-shaped hole where the no-code widget should be.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Senja
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Polished and genuinely free, right up to testimonial number sixteen; the core collection job then becomes paid.

notes: Free and uncapped for one site, so the build is a hobby rather than a saving · the badge on the collection page is the one real reason to self-host.
prompt:
Build me a testimonial collection and display tool. Requirements:

- Stack: one Node + TypeScript service (Fastify) with SQLite via better-sqlite3 and local disk
  for uploads. No Docker, no separate frontend build, no customer accounts.
- A public collection page at /c/:slug · name, role, company, avatar upload, 1-5 star rating,
  and the quote. Each field individually toggleable per project from a config row. Submissions
  land as pending. Show a thank-you state after submit.
- An /admin page behind basic auth from .env: pending queue with approve/reject, plus pin and
  delete on approved ones. Nothing is public until approved.
- An embeddable wall: GET /widget.js injects the approved testimonials into any page via one
  script tag plus a div, rendered into a shadow DOM so the host page's CSS can't leak in.
  No iframe.
- Offer three layouts (masonry, single-column list, horizontal carousel) and read layout,
  accent colour, light/dark theme and card corner radius from data- attributes on the tag.
- Server-render the widget HTML and have the script fetch it, so the testimonials are in the
  response rather than assembled client-side. Cache it with a short max-age plus
  stale-while-revalidate.
- Render every approved card in that response and hide the ones past a configurable initial
  count, then have Load More just unhide them · no second request, one paint, and the full set
  is in the HTML for crawlers.
- Drive all sizing from CSS custom properties on the container rather than per-element inline
  styles, so one stylesheet covers every layout and card style.
- Avatars resized server-side to 128px squares on upload with sharp; reject files over 5MB.
- Count impressions and click-throughs in SQLite · fire an impression only after the wall has
  been intersecting for one second, latch it so it can't fire twice per page load, and filter
  obvious bot user agents server-side.
- Rate-limit submissions per IP and add a honeypot field, because a public form will get spam.
- Ship a README with the paste-in snippet and VPS deploy steps behind TLS.
- Deliberately out of scope: video testimonials, importing from other platforms, team seats,
  and email notifications.
